questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I would consider both academic opportunities and the exploration of new cultures as two of the same thing since  I am musicology student and therefore a student of humanities, history and culture. Scotland is one of those countries where the culture and history is most evidently intertwined which is especially evident in the folk music tradition. So that is why I chose Scotland.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The vast amount of websides, mails etc. made it very unclear which things actually was important to bring. Mobility online, Erasmus+ and OLA is really over complicated in my opinion.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Advice by mail.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very f****** difficult. I ended up paying much more than I initially had planned on accomodation and it was only just ten days before my arrival, that I managed to find something, which was way over budget. The university service did no help whatsoever except a "guidance on the private marked". I spend almost six months looking endlessly to find something and that alone is a reason why I would not necessarily recommend others to go to Edinburgh as an exchange student for one semester. Many of my "co-exange students" from Copenhagen managed to get student accomodation by calling the service all the time. It was up sheer luck whether someone got a room or not. However I ended up living with a lovely old grandma, who definitely contributed positively to my overall experience, but I could have done without the long time spend on accomodation.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Does not really matter if you live on or of campus. There are experiences to be gained either way.

questions.answer: UCPH is way more critical in its teaching approaches, which is something I sometimes missed in Edinburgh, where it was much more: "Here is the facts".

questions.answer: Choir and hillwalking

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Not that difficult. Scotland and Denmark are not that different culturally. The only thing was to learn how to express your feelings and the everyday life in English.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness and kindness of Scottish people <3

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Embrace the crisis - eventually you will feel a bit lost in a foreign country, That's not dangerous. Its just change and knowledge setting in

Travel outside the city! Take any opportunity to get out to nature  

Spend time alone - learn to do things that are good for you by yourself.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Remove the strict rules about attendance... That was really limiting as an exchange student trying to make the most of it.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to learn about yourself. And also walks in mountains

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The fact that most UK-students are younger than DK-students. And also being "exposed" to the open world, which is the thing you learn the most from!

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
